title: Protocol for Oredsson Universal Replacement Medium for Cell Banking and Culturing
author: Oredsson, Malakpour-Permlid, et al.
materials: The procedures presented below are for solutions used in the protocols described in step-by-step method details.15.Prepare 25 mL of a solution containing 1 mg HSA/mL PBS.a.Pipette 12.5 mL PBS to a 50 mL test tube.b.Add 12.5 mL of the solution containing 2 mg HSA/mL PBS to the test tube.c.Sterile filter the solution and label the test tube: 1 mg HSA/mL PBS.16.Prepare 5 mL 100 mM acetic acid from 100% acetic acid, which is equivalent to 17.41 M.a.Add 4971.3 μL Millipore H2O to a test tube labeled 100 mM acetic acid.b.Add 28.7 μL of 100% acetic acid to the test tube.17.Centrifuge the vial with IL-2 at 200–300 g before opening in the LAF bench.18.Reconstitute 10 μg of IL-2 in 50 μL of 100 mM acetic acid.19.Add 0.450 mL of PBS containing 1 mg HSA/mL to the vial.20.Transfer the solution to a 15 mL test tube.21.Add 0.5 mL PBS containing 1 mg HSA/mL to the vial.22.Transfer to the test tube.23.Repeat step 7 eight more times until the final volume of 5 mL is reached24.Sterile filter the final solution.25.Aliquot the solution in sterile labeled Eppendorf tubes.26.Store the aliquots at −80°C.Note: Reconstituted IL-2 can be stored at −80°C for one year according to the manufactureŕs instructions. We recommend using HSA instead of bovine serum albumin as suggested in the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare PBS with HSA
steps.instruction: Make sterile PBS solutions containing human serum albumin (HSA) for thawing and freezing steps.

substeps.instruction: Add 150 mL sterile PBS (20‑25 °C) to a sterile 500 mL bottle, add 6 g HSA, then add 50 mL sterile PBS; rock gently until fully dissolved (≈1 h). Sterile‑filter (0.22 µm), aliquot 10 mL into sterile 50 mL tubes, label “Human Serum Albumin, 30 mg/mL PBS”, and store at –20 °C (final volume 200 mL, 30 mg/mL HSA).

Add 300 mL sterile PBS (20‑25 °C) to a sterile 500 mL bottle, add 1.6 g HSA, then add 100 mL sterile PBS; rock gently until fully dissolved (≈1 h). Sterile‑filter (0.22 µm), aliquot 20 mL into sterile 50 mL tubes, label “Human Serum Albumin, 2 mg/mL PBS”, and store at –20 °C (final volume 400 mL, 2 mg/mL HSA).

steps.title: Prepare IL‑2 stock solution
steps.instruction: Generate a 2 ng µL⁻¹ IL‑2 solution in HSA‑PBS for T‑cell culture.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 25 mL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ HSA in PBS: mix 12.5 mL PBS with 12.5 mL of the 2 mg mL⁻¹ HSA/PBS solution, sterile‑filter, and label “1 mg HSA/mL PBS”.
Prepare 5 mL of 100 mM acetic acid: add 4 971.3 µL sterile water to a tube, then add 28.7 µL glacial acetic acid; mix.
Centrifuge the IL‑2 vial at 200–300 g for a few seconds in a LAF bench before opening.
Reconstitute 10 µg IL‑2 in 50 µL of the 100 mM acetic acid solution.
Add 0.450 mL of the 1 mg HSA/mL PBS to the IL‑2 vial, mix, and transfer the mixture to a 15 mL tube.
Add 0.500 mL of the 1 mg HSA/mL PBS to the vial, mix, and transfer to the same tube.
Repeat the addition of 0.500 mL PBS‑HSA and transfer eight more times (total 9 additions) until the final volume reaches 5 mL.
Sterile‑filter the final 5 mL solution, aliquot into labeled sterile Eppendorf tubes, and store at –80 °C (stable for 1 year).

steps.title: Prepare suspension‑culture OUR medium
steps.instruction: Formulate OUR medium for suspension cultures by following the published recipe with two modifications.

substeps.instruction: Follow the published OUR medium formulation (Weber et al.) but replace the basal medium DMEM/F12 with RPMI 1640.
Omit all attachment proteins (collagen, fibronectin, vitronectin, laminin, fetuin A) from the formulation.

steps.title: Thaw cryopreserved cells
steps.instruction: Recover cells from liquid‑nitrogen storage with minimal DMSO exposure.

substeps.instruction: Warm PBS‑30 mg/mL HSA, PBS‑2 mg/mL HSA, and OUR medium to the indicated temperatures (PBS to 20‑25 °C, OUR medium to 37 °C).
Heat a water bath to 37 °C.
Retrieve the cryovial, place it in the 37 °C water bath, and thaw for 1.5–2 min until a small ice chunk remains, shaking slowly.
Transfer the thawed content to a sterile 50 mL tube.
Add 2 mL PBS‑30 mg/mL HSA over 2 min (1 mL min⁻¹) while gently shaking.
Add 8 mL PBS‑2 mg/mL HSA over 8 min (1 mL min⁻¹) while gently shaking (slow DMSO dilution).
Add additional PBS to bring the total volume to 40 mL.
Centrifuge at 200–300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 5–7 mL OUR medium (volume adjusted to cell count).
Take an aliquot with a sterile Pasteur pipette, load a hemocytometer, and count cells (use viability stain if needed).
Calculate cell concentration.
For adherent lines, seed cells on Corning Primaria plastic pre‑coated with fibronectin using OUR medium.
For suspension lines, seed cells in the suspension‑culture OUR medium in any tissue‑culture flask.

steps.title: Detach adherent cells
steps.instruction: Release cells from culture vessels using TrypLE Select and HSA‑PBS.

substeps.instruction: Warm PBS‑2 mg/mL HSA to 20‑25 °C.
Warm TrypLE Select and PBS to 20‑25 °C.
Warm OUR medium to 37 °C.
Aspirate existing medium from the flask.
Rinse the cell layer with PBS‑2 mg/mL HSA (0.2 mL cm⁻²; e.g., 5 mL for a 25 cm² flask) and aspirate the rinse.
Add TrypLE Select (40 µL cm⁻²; e.g., 1 mL for a 25 cm² flask) and ensure even coverage.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 min (monitor under a microscope).
If cells are not fully detached, gently tap the flask.
Add PBS‑2 mg/mL HSA at 5 mL per mL of TrypLE Select (e.g., 5 mL for 1 mL TrypLE) and slowly triturate to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Transfer the suspension to a labeled sterile tube (15 mL or 50 mL as appropriate).
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in OUR medium supplemented with fibronectin (volume sufficient for counting).
Take an aliquot for cell counting, load a hemocytometer, count, and calculate concentration.

steps.title: Seed cells with fibronectin
steps.instruction: Plate counted cells onto tissue‑culture vessels using OUR medium containing fibronectin.

substeps.instruction: Determine the desired cells cm⁻² and calculate the required suspension volume.
For a 25 cm² flask, add 4–4.5 mL of OUR medium (including the cell suspension).
Add medium to the flask first and incubate 10 min to allow attachment‑protein binding and temperature/pH equilibration.
Add the calculated cell suspension to reach the target final volume and cell density.
Mix gently with an “8” motion.
Place the flask in a 5 % CO₂ incubator (37 °C).
Unscrew the lid slightly to permit gas exchange if the flask lacks a filter.

steps.title: Renew medium without fibronectin
steps.instruction: Replace spent medium with fibronectin‑free OUR medium.

substeps.instruction: Warm fibronectin‑free OUR medium to 37 °C.
Aspirate the old medium carefully without disturbing the cell monolayer.
Add the same volume of the pre‑warmed fibronectin‑free medium along the side of the flask to minimize disturbance.
Return the flask to the CO₂ incubator and unscrew the lid slightly for gas exchange.
For cultures kept ≥1 week, perform this renewal every 3–4 days.

steps.title: Freeze cell suspension
steps.instruction: Cryopreserve cells in PBS‑HSA with 5 % DMSO.

substeps.instruction: Thaw PBS‑30 mg/mL HSA and warm to 20‑25 °C.
After detachment, determine total cell number (use the count from the detachment step).
Centrifuge at 200–300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in PBS‑30 mg/mL HSA at 2 × 10⁶ cells per 1 425 µL.
Label cryotubes with cell line, passage number, and date.
Add 75 µL DMSO to each 1 425 µL cell suspension (final DMSO = 5 %).
Mix gently and transfer the mixture to a 1.5 mL cryotube (final volume 1.5 mL).
Place cryotubes in a controlled‑rate freezing container (e.g., Mr. Frosty) and store at –80 °C for ≥24 h.
Transfer the vials to liquid‑nitrogen storage for long‑term preservation.

steps.title: Thaw and culture VERO/A549 cells
steps.instruction: Demonstrate routine thaw‑seed‑culture‑freeze workflow for VERO and A549 lines.

substeps.instruction: Thaw VERO (ATCC) or A549 (ECACC) cells using the “Thaw cryopreserved cells” protocol.
Seed the thawed cells into a 25 cm² Primaria flask (label with cell line, p1, date).
Incubate for 4 days in the incubator.
Detach cells using the “Detach adherent cells” protocol.
Count cells and calculate the volume needed to seed at 25 000 cells cm⁻².
Seed the calculated volume into the appropriate number of flasks.
Label flasks with cell line, p2, and date.
Change medium (fibronectin‑free) after 3–4 days.
Detach cells again 7 days after the initial seeding and repeat the routine.
Use the expanded cells for downstream experiments.
When needed, freeze cells following the “Freeze cell suspension” protocol to generate a new stock.

steps.title: Generate growth curves for THP‑1/Jurkat
steps.instruction: Measure proliferation of suspension‑culture cells in OUR medium over four days.

substeps.instruction: Label three 25 cm² tissue‑culture flasks with the cell line name and numbers 1, 2, 3.
Add 4 mL of OUR medium for suspension culture to each flask and equilibrate in the incubator for 30 min (loosen caps).
Determine the current cell concentration of the routine THP‑1 or Jurkat culture (sample with a sterile Pasteur pipette and count in a hemocytometer).
Prepare a 5 mL cell suspension at 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in OUR suspension medium.
Add 1 mL of this suspension to each flask, mix gently, and return flasks to the incubator (caps loosened).
On days 1‑4, sequentially remove one flask, gently mix its contents, withdraw a sample with a sterile Pasteur pipette, and count cells in a hemocytometer.
Immediately return the remaining flasks to the incubator.
Plot cell number versus time to obtain growth curves (mean ± SD from the three flasks).
